chunks: Verily the life of this world is no more than a sport and frivolity. If you believe and fear God, he will give you your reward, and will not ask for your possessions.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between faith, God-consciousness, and worldly wealth in this Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies that the 'play' of the world is not inherently sinful but becomes so when it distracts from the Hereafter; it assures believers that sincere faith and piety do not necessitate the forfeiture of their worldly wealth, distinguishing true devotion from asceticism. This perspective is often linked to the concept of 'not being asked' for wealth as a penalty for sin, but rather retaining it as a trust while receiving full spiritual recompense. The verse thus encourages a balanced life where material resources are utilized in the path of God without attachment.
